article_framing_rejections.headline: Infant death investigation reveals messages warning father baby was starving

lead_independence.headline: Infant death investigation reveals messages warning father baby was starving
lead_independence.lead: Text messages obtained during the investigation into the death of a 3-month-old infant in Fort Pierce showed family members repeatedly warning both parents that something was wrong. On August 12, 2025, messages sent to Nicole Maxwell stated, 'The baby's got nothing to eat. I don't know what to give him.' Days later, additional messages warned that the baby was sick, covered in marks and sleeping constantly. Other messages urged Jason Gunter to come to Florida because something was wrong with the infant. According to detectives, neither parent took action that resulted in immediate medical care for the child.

source_focus.source_lead: A fourth person has been arrested in connection with the death of a 3-month-old baby who allegedly died from severe dehydration and malnutrition. lead_independence.headline: Fort Pierce woman faces fraud charges as search warrant executed at Indian River Estates home
lead_independence.lead: Crime scene investigators were seen outside Grasso's home in the Indian River Estates neighborhood near Sunset Boulevard as deputies served a search warrant connected to the ongoing Southern Truss fraud investigation. Grasso, who worked as the company's bookkeeper and comptroller, was arrested July 16 along with Sheri Lynn Harrs and Tina Marie Mejia. Grasso faces charges of first-degree grand theft of $100,000 or more, organized fraud of $50,000 or more, racketeering and money laundering of $100,000 or more. Harrs and Mejia each face charges of grand theft, organized fraud and racketeering. Grasso has pleaded not guilty, and her bond was set at a combined $1.15 million.
